b: Nearly every landmark deal (HPS, Angelo Gordon, Monroe) is about buying credit capability. Banks retreated; managers are racing to own the lending economics. Good news for a credit-anchored newcomer: the strategy is where capital wants to be.

h: Scale or specialise — the middle is dying
b: Mega-managers consolidate to amortise distribution, data and compliance costs; specialist boutiques thrive on edge. Mid-size generalists get bought or squeezed. Our answer must be specialisation (maritime, healthcare/deeptech, diaspora capital) — not scale.

h: Data and software are strategic assets
b: BlackRock owning Aladdin + eFront + Preqin means one firm supplies the industry's operating system and its benchmark data. Expect data advantage to shape fundraising: managers who instrument their portfolios well will raise faster.

h: The wealth channel is the new LP
b: iCapital-style feeders, evergreen and semi-liquid funds are opening private markets to advisers and UHNW clients. Distribution partnerships (private banks, platforms) now drive AUM growth as much as institutional sales — directly relevant to our private-bank feeder plans.
Minority GP-stake investors (Blue Owl, Petershill, Hunter Point) let founders monetise without losing control — the exit-and-growth route most likely relevant to a manager like ours in 5–7 years.
Apollo-Athene's model — permanent insurance capital feeding origination — is being copied across the industry. Managers with guaranteed capital bases out-compete pure fundraisers on stability.
